lectures.title: Religious and social reform movements in Andhra

parts.t: Kandukuri Veeresalingam and the Telugu Renaissance
items: **Father of the Telugu Renaissance Movement:** **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** (Telugu Renaissance / Social Reform).
**First widow remarriage in Andhra:** 11 Dec 1881, at Rajahmundry (Veeresalingam).
**Vivekavardhini Patasala / Sangham:** founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874 at Rajahmundry; rationalism + female literacy + anti-caste.
**Rajasekhara Charitram / Charithram:** the first novel in Telugu, written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam.

parts.t: Brahma Samaj and Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu
items: Responsible for spread of the idea
**Brahma Prakasika:** journal, 1886; editor Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Bhogam:** caste that disappeared from Andhra society due to the efforts of Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Mahaboob College:** saved by Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu as Principal before Independence.
**Adi Hindu Social Service League:** founded by **Bhagya Reddy Verma**.
**Andhra Pitamaha:** Madapati Hanumantha Rao is called / known as Andhra Pitamaha.
**People's Dialect Movement (Telugu):** **Gidugu Rama Murthy** is the father of the movement for people's dialect in Telugu.
**First book printed in Telugu:** The Bible.
Gurram Jashuva (modern poet; his famous work)
**Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam:** Hyderabad, 1901; founded by Komarraju Lakshmana Rao (K.V. Lakshmana Rao + associates).
**Its place:** first Telugu library in Hyderabad; 1st non-govt public Telugu library in Telangana / Hyderabad; set up to develop Telugu language & literature in Telangana.
**Vignana Chandrika Mandali:** Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao (K.V. Lakshmana Rao) + associates, 1906, Hyderabad; popular science / history / political literature in Telugu.
**Andhra Samvardhani Granthalayam:** 1905, Secunderabad; an early Telugu library.
**"The Library Movement in Andhra is Swayambhu."** Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah (I.V. Ramanaiah), on the Andhra Library Movement.
Publisher of the first Telugu journal Satyadoota
Christian Association of Bellary; published from Bellary
Founded by A.P. Partha Sarathi Naidu, who was also its editor

parts.t: Other journals, newspapers and their editors
items: Konda Venkatappayya (one of the founders & first editor); Mutnuri Krishna Rao was its later editor
Strongly supported the Home Rule Movement
Commented on the need for a separate government for Telugu culture
Founded and edited by Shabnavis Venkata Rama Narasimha Rao
Associated with N.G. Ranga and peasant leaders
